Commentary.Commentary: Glenn Maxwell and Ashton Agar were the star players for Australia. The former got some shots from the middle of the bat and gave a scare to the English bowlers in the middle overs. Agar accompanied him and together they tried to steer their sinking ship out of the water with a 84-run partnership. Considering the conditions, adaptability and their form, it should be an easy outing for the England batsmen. However, one can never consider Australia out of the competition. Join us on the other side of the innings break.

First innings belongs to the home team. They have managed to topple Australia for 214 and haven't even allowed them to play their full quota of 50 overs. David Willey got the first wicket in the second over of the match and afterwards, it was Moeen Ali show. His spell of 3/43 meant that the top order of the visiting team couldn't get hold of him. He, along with Adil Rashid, made sure that no easy runs were given. The batsmen, in order to get some quick runs, started manufacturing shots and ended up giving away their wickets cheaply.

OUT! A good low catch by the keeper. Another slower one by Liam, it's in the line of the stumps as Tye hops back to make some room. He ends up reaching out for it and edging it behind to the keeper. It's dying in front of Buttler who does well to go down low to catch it inches above the ground. Third wicket for Plunkett and AUSTRALIA ARE BUNDLED OUT FOR 214!
Some change in pace there to fox the batsman. Tye tries to flick by moving back but misses. He is hit on the back leg as the ball rolls to point.
SIX! Ho! Ho! Ho! Take that for a reply. The blow on the helmet seems to have woken Tye up. He hangs back on the back foot, waits for the ball to arrive and launches it over mid-wicket for a biggie.

Physio comes out to the middle. Andrew Tye seems fine and is smiling. Sipping some water and trying to regain his composure. A little bit of repair work going on his helmet. He is a bowler so probably hasn't carried a spare one.

That's hit Tye on the helmet! Another short ball by Plunkett, targeted at the head of the batsman, who tries to pull but misses. It hits him on the hand and then goes bang on the grille of the helmet. Tye immediately gives thumbs up signalling his well being.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Digs in a short ball, nicely directed at the batsman, Tye sways away from the line of fire.
Another yorker from Wood. Stanlake gets under it and manages to keep it out.
On a good length, outside off and Billy dabs it to the point region for nothing.
Yorker to start with to Billy, who does well to keep it out.

OUT! Another soft dismissal and another catch for the English Test skipper, Joe Root. Full and on the stumps from Wood, Kane goes for the big shot but doesn't get the elevation. Joe Root at mid off takes an easy catch. Ninth wicket down for Australia.
Another short delivery, this time Tye plays it to mid on and runs for a single.
Short of a length, coming into the body with pace. The batsman does well to keep it down towards the mid-wicket region.
Mark Wood is back into the attack.

Kumar Sangakkara (on air) giving his inputs on how to play the spinners. He shares that while growing up back home he used to concentrate on the bowling hand to read the variations and doesn't forget to add that there were quite a few with unorthodox action. Goes on to advice that nowadays with so many variety of wrist spinners coming up, the batsmen need to sit back and analyze their action before facing them, rather than trying to pick them from the surface.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Another bumper from the bowler. Kane was in two minds but chooses to leave the ball alone.
Plunkett goes short and the batsman ducks under it.
Cross-seam delivery outside off and Kane dabs it to backward point.
A fuller delivery on off and the batsman drives to covers for nothing.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. They pick up a single
Loopy flighted delivery just outside off, Kane goes for the big hit but misses to make connection with the ball.
Wide! Goes down the leg side and the batsman tries to get something on it but misses. Wide signalled by the umpire.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Fuller and wider, Tye gets down on his knee and creams the drive through covers. One run added to the total.
A flighted delivery from Rashid just outside off and Tye goes for a wild hoick but miscues. The ball goes over Root stationed at first slip and the batsmen take two.
Gives it air and lets it rip on middle, the batsman nudges it through mid-wicket and takes a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Bouncer! Plunkett goes short and Tye ducks under the ball to let it pass.
Stays put in his crease and blocks the fuller delivery.
FOUR! SHOT! Tye gets a full ball, on the off stump and drives it uppishly through the line over the bowler's head. The ball races down the ground and into the boundary.
Kane Richardson is the next batsman in.

OUT! Australia have lost their eighth wicket. Full and outside off from Plunkett and Neser goes with hard hands. He tries to hit it over the bowler's head but gets it from the outside half of the bat. The ball lobs in the air and Joe Root at mid off takes an easy catch. Another soft dismissal.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Liam Plunkett is back into the attack.
Tossed up and on off, defended off the front foot.
Shout for an lbw, not given. Skidding down the leg side, Tye fails to flick and is hit on the pads. The appeal is not entertained as it seemed to be missing leg.
Tye has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Wow, that came from nowhere. A quicker one, darted in on the fuller length, Tye covers the line and smacks it over the bowler's head. This is also the first boundary conceded by Rashid today. Considering he is a leg spinner, who usually conceded too many boundary balls, that's a commendable effort.
Flatter and on off, Tye defends it back off his back foot.
Andrew Tye is the new batsman.

OUT! Rashid strikes and removes the set batsman. He bowls this leg spinner quicker through the air, a scrambled seam delivery which is served very full and around off. Agar tries to sweep but misses and is hit on the back leg. They appeal and the finger goes up almost immediately. Agar has a chat with his partner before trudging back. The replays show that it's pretty adjacent and would have crashed into the stumps. Australia losing the plot towards the end.
Full and on the pads and timed to mid on for another single.
Short and climbing on Agar, who does well to keep it down off the back foot.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Touch fuller and driven to the mid on region for a single.
Full and angling into the batsman, who drills it uppishly to mid on.
On a good length and on off, the batsman drives it through mid on for nothing.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.
Floated leg spinner from Rashid and Neser played it nicely through covers for two amidst some hesitation.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Proper leg spinning delivery, outside off and Neser drives it through covers for nothing.
OHH! A googly and almost got his man. Rashid is toying with the debutant. Flighted outside off and the batsman gets the inside edge of the bat on to his pads.
Flighted outside off and driven through mid off for nothing.
Full and coming in to the batsman, Agar guides it to the mid-wicket fielder for nothing.

FOUR! Copy paste stuff from Agar! Marvelous timing! Gets the full delivery outside off and Agar presents the full face of the bat. The ball meets the middle and rushes through covers and mid off regions for the second boundary of the over.
Short and outside off, Neser punches it off the back foot to the off side and takes a single.
Full and straight and driven through mid on by Agar. One run added to the total.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.

FOUR! Stand and deliver is the method for Agar. Willey bowls it full, just outside off and Agar plays it through the line and finds the gap between the cover and mid off regions. Authoritative batting from the left-hander.
Lots of rips on this one by Adil. The ball pitches on off and spins away from  the batsman. He gets behind the line and blocks it nicely.
Driven towards the mid off region. They pick up a single.
First runs in international cricket for Neser. Touch short and flatter, the batsman plays it through the point region for another single.
Floats it on middle and the batsman drives it through mid on for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on off, the batsman blocks it from his crease with a straight bat.
Adil Rashid is back into the attack.
Full on leg stump and tucked away to fine leg for a single.
Debutant Michael Neser is the new batsman.

OUT! The Big Show is gone! Huge, huge wicket for England. He was looking in ominous touch. Liam bowls it on a back of a length, angling into the body and Maxwell picked it beautifully off his hips. But the ball hangs in the air and Bairstow comes running across to his right from deep square leg to complete the catch easily. A nothing delivery gets an important wicket. After a series of failures, this knock will give immense confidence to Maxwell, although Australia would have loved him to carry till the end.
The batsman has driven fuller ball straight back.
Touch wide and back of a length, the batsman plays it through the off side. The ball goes through the cover region and they take two.
Similar delivery and Agar does well to punch it off the back foot through covers for another single.
Short of a length on off, Maxwell flicks it to the deep backward square leg and takes a single.
Forces a shortish ball square of the wicket on the off side and takes a single.

Aggression shown by Willey! Shortish length ball just outside off, Maxwell punches it straight back to the bowler who picks it up and has an immediate shy at the striker's end. Maxwell just escapes from getting hit. Hmm...
An overpitched delivery outside off has been crunched through covers. The sweeper cuts it off and they take a single.
Back of a length delivery around middle and leg, a slower one, Maxwell goes on his toes and turns it in front of square leg for a single.

Sliding down the leg side, Maxwell tries to flick but misses. It goes off his pads to short fine leg. He thinks about taking a leg bye but then decides against it as the fielder at 45 quickly gets to the ball.
Angles in a length ball on off, Agar bunts it down to long on and takes a single.
David Willey is back into the attack.
Fullish and angling down the leg side, Maxwell nudges it down to fine leg and scampers back for the second run. Could have been close but the throw from the deep wasn't an accurate one.

FOUR! Well placed! It's short and around off, Maxwell swivels on the back foot and just gives the direction to his pull shot. It runs through backward square leg and finds the fence. Didn't try to hit that hard and that was the key. You don't normally associate Maxwell with that kind of a shot.
A little bit of width on offer outside off, Agar steers it through the point region and picks up a single.
This one is full and around middle, angling away with some extra bounce, Agar gets forward and pushes it down to mid off.
Wicket to wicket line, on a length, Agar blocks it back from the crease.
On a length and in the line of the stumps, Agar covers the line and pushes it down the ground to mid off.
Wide! Short but down the leg side, Agar ducks to let that one go to the keeper.
A touch straight from Wood and tucked away down the leg side for another single.
Another short delivery and pulled away from the splice. The ball goes to the mid-wicket region and the batsmen scamper for two.
On a good length, on the off stump and Agar blocks it off the front foot.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
Short delivery pulled away to backward square. One run added to the total.
On a good length, hits Maxwell on his pads. Some appeal from the bowler as well as the fielder but umpire isn't interested. Too high and missing leg too, the replays showed later.
Drives through mid on but straight to mid on.
Short of a length, outside off and the batsman dabs it to the point region fro nothing.

FOUR! Another good looking shot from Agar. He is playing a crucial knock for his team and providing company to Maxwell. Touch short and outside off, Agar gets on top of the bounce and chops it through the point region for another boundary.
Dabs it to the point region for nothing.

FOUR! How good is that from the left-hander? Liam bowls it on a good length on middle and off, Agar plays through the line and gets it past the fielder at mid on. The ball has enough legs to go to the boundary.
Short on leg, Maxi flicks it to the mid-wicket region and takes a single. With this single, he brings up his 16th half century in ODIs as well. A much-needed knock for Australia.
Drives the fuller delivery through mid off for nothing.
Touch short and into the body, Agar punches it off the back foot.
A bumper from Wood and Agar is happy to leave the short ball alone.
Effort ball this one from Wood. Just short of a length, outside off and making the batsman play at it but Agar misses.
Slower delivery on middle and off, the batsman guides it to the mid on region for a single.
Full and outside off, Maxwell drives it off the front foot but straight to the mid off fielder.
Short and outside off, Agar chops it hard and gets it over the point fielder. Before the ball is thrown back from the deep, the batsmen managed to come back for the second.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball for nothing.
Short of a length, coming into the batsman. Maxwell guides it to mid-wicket for another single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
50-run partnership. A crucial stand for the Aussies. A short delivery outside off and the batsman guides it past the point fielder and takes a single.
Starts with a short delivery to Maxwell, who looks to force it but doesn't get the connection.
Touch short, on middle and tucked away to the point region for nothing.
Another bouncer and another nice leave from the left-hander.
Bouncer from Wood and Agar is happy to duck under it.

Nasser Hussain trying to analyze Adil Rashid's bowling action. He identifies that it's quite tough to pick him from the hand as he bowls with a quick-arm action. Nass feels that the batsmen try to pick him through the trajectory in which he lands the ball. If it's around leg, they assume it to be a leg spinner and if it's outside off, they assume it to be a googly. He is quick to add though that it's not the best way to play the leggie as he can bowl other variations apart from the above ones.
Short of a length outside the off stump and Maxwell punches it through covers for a single.
Touch short and outside off. Agar plays it through mid-wicket and takes a single.
On a good length on off, Agar plays it to the mid on region.
Mark Wood is back into the attack.

FOUR! How beautifully timed is that! Liam bowls a fuller one on his pads and Maxwell obliges. He clips it off his pads and the fielder at mid-wicket has no chance of stopping it, even after he puts in the dive.

Just before the 14-run over by Moeen, there was a little drinks break taken by the batsmen. Probably, the message to Maxwell was to go after the bowlers and since then the approach has changed. 25 runs followed in the next two overs. The current one although has brought the sanity back in England's favour.
Fuller in length, outside off, Maxwell plays it to the mid on region.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back.
Touch short and angling into the body, Maxwell stays on the back foot and defends it.
Similar looking delivery and the batsman gets behind to block it for nothing.
On a good length just outside off, Maxwell punches it back to the bowler.
Liam Plunkett is into the attack for the first time today.
Plays the floated delivery to the square leg region and takes the strike for the next over.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.

Wide! Mind games! Root saw Maxwell is looking to make room for himself, so he tries to target his pads. But the batsman has played with the bowler here as he moved inside the line and let the ball go down the leg side for a wide.
Punches the fuller delivery from the front foot. The ball goes past the short cover fielder. Another run added to the total.
Plays the flighted delivery to the mid-wicket region and takes a single.
SIX! Bang! Brute force from Maxi. He gets the flighted delivery outside off and punches it up and over the mid off region. No half measures there.
Pushed in with the arm by Root and the batsman drives it to the mid off region for a single.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. No run to end the over. 14 coming off it and spoils Moeen's bowling figures a bit. Still 10-1-43-3 is a mighty good effort by the off spinner.
SIX! Goes big and sends it over the rope. Another flighted ball around off, too full in length and Maxwell lifts it with nice timing over wide long off for a maximum.
Tossed up and on off, blocked by Maxwell.
FOUR! Maxwell is changing gears, it seems. Moeen is on the shorter side, around middle and Maxwell plays a thunderous pull shot to the deep square leg fence. No chance for the fielder in the deep.
FOUR! Maxwell takes the aerial route. Goes deep inside the crease to a full ball and lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Short and on off, punched off the back foot but straight to the cover fielder.
Plays it with the spin in front of square leg and keeps strike with a single.
Floated full on middle, it's driven down to long off for a single.
Flatter on middle, helped to mid-wicket.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Gets forward to a full ball and drills it down to long off for one.
Fires one in from around the wicket, it's on middle and Agar keeps it out on the leg side. Straight to mid-wicket.
Another flighted delivery to end the spell. Agar rocks to the back foot and punches it through covers for a single.
Quicker delivery from Ali and the batsman gets behind the line to block it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floated on off and Agar drives it straight back to the bowler.
The ball grips and turns from the off stump and the batsman plays it with spin off his pads. They take a single.
Floated on middle and leg. Maxwell plays it to mid-wicket.
Another solid looking defense from Agar to end the over.
Gets behind the line of the arm delivery on off stump and blocks it down.
Flighted and spinning away from the left-hander who punches it towards the mid-wicket region for nothing.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single.
Another powerful punch form the back foot, this time through covers and another two runs added to the total.
Tucks the shortish delivery away to the mid-wicket region. The fielder does well but can't stop them from taking a double.
Joe Root is into the attack.
Shuffles across his stumps and sweeps it to the square leg region. Takes a single to end the over.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it down the pitch.
Punches the ball past the bowler. Takes a single from the mid  off region.
Drives the flighted delivery straight back to the bowler.
Rocks back and forces the ball to the mid off region. One run added to the total.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floated and on off, driven down to mid off to end the over.
Tickles it off his pads to the leg side, finds the gap and takes a run.
Flatter and on off, spinning away a shade, Maxwell initially shapes up for the slog sweep but then changes his mind after not finding the delivery in his half. Ends up forcing it out towards covers.
Full and flighted outside off, Agar calmly pushes it down to long off for a single.
Goes on the back foot and punches it down to point for one.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Maiden over. Ali has been so good since his first over and has continued his merry ways. Another one played to the mid-wicket region for nothing.
Goes back in his crease and blocks it from the back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Punches the ball from the back foot.
Defends it off the back foot. More pressure building up.
Plays the ball with a straight bat for nothing.
Another loopy one from Adil and Agar plays it back to the bowler.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground.
Ashton Agar is the new batsman in.

OUT! Googly has done the job for the leg spinner. Half the side is back in the hut for Australia. This is not looking good for them. Stoinis is walking back with a look of disbelief. He thought the wide and shortish delivery was an opportunity to get some runs but it was a bit too close for the square cut. He went with hard hands and only managed an edge. Buttler takes it easily and jumps in celebration.
Driven towards the mid on region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Drives to mid off from the front foot and takes a single.
The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man for nothing.
Maxwell plays the wristy shot to the leg side and scampers for quick double.
The ball takes the outside edge goes towards the slip region. One run added to the total.
SIX! High and handsome! Stoinis gives the charge to the flighted delivery, picks it over the long on fielder and the ball lands in the crowd way behind. Welcome runs for Stoinis and Australia.
Ali pushes the ball into the stumps and the batsman blocks it with the straight bat.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Shuffles to the off side to play the sweep to the leg side. The ball rolls to the square leg and they take two.
Punches the ball to the off side and gets another single.
Driven towards the mid on region. One run added to the total.
Punches the flighted delivery outside off from the crease and takes a single.
Rocks on the back foot and dabs it to the cover region for a single.
Plants his foot down the pitch and guides the ball to the off side for a single.
Tossed up outside off and Stoinis lets it go.
Forces a full ball down to mid on to end another tidy over by Moeen. 2 runs and a wicket from it!
Brings out the sweep shot this time. He gets across the stumps to execute that but misses to wear it on his pads. Only a stifled appeal for an lbw. Impact well outside off.
Tossed up ball landing just outside off and spinning back in a touch, Maxwell gets forward and across to flick but closes the face of the bat early. It goes off the leading edge to covers.
Helps it off his pads to the leg side but finds the square leg fielder.

Loopy full on off, spinning back in, Maxwell gets forward and works it off the inner half of the bat towards mid-wicket. The fielder there dives to his right but fails to cut it off. They take a couple.

Drinks are on the field. England are the happier side going into the break. They have Australia's top order in the kitty and Moeen Ali is proving too difficult to score runs off. Although some bad shots from the Aussies resulted in their wickets, it's the pressure created by good bowling from the home team's bowlers.

OUT! Four down, Australia. Now they lose their skipper as well. Moeen Ali continues with his good work. He is ripping through the Aussie line-up. Tim Paine is the victim this time. Moeen flights the ball on off stump and Paine goes for the reverse sweep. But he gets a top edge and goes straight to Mark Wood at short third man. Too easy for the number one team right now.
Too full and outside off, Stoinis powers his drive down to wide long off for a brace.
Loopy and on off, tapped towards covers for a single.
Flighted and outside off, left alone.
Gets on the front foot and drives it to covers.
Tossed up on off, driven past the bowler to long off for one.
Takes a stride forward to a full ball and plays it off the outside half of the bat to point. A single taken.
Fullish and on off, defended off the front foot towards the bowler. England keeping things tight and building nice pressure on the Aussies.
Walks forward to work it on the leg side but it takes the outer half of the bat and rolls towards mid off.
Stoinis has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. Tidy stuff from Moeen!
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Flatter and on middle, forced down the ground for a run.
Flighted and full outside off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Driven towards the mid off region. They pick up a single.
The batsman has driven it through mid on for nothing.
OOH! So close to the off stump. Gives the ball enough air and keeps it on off stump. Paine goes with the straight bat but misses it as the ball thuds into the keeper's hands.
Works the loopy delivery down the leg side. One run added to the total.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Punches it to covers from the back foot and takes a single.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
Rocks back and punches the ball down the ground for another single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Drives the flighted delivery through the mid on region.
Dabs it through the point region for a single.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Another resolute defense as Australia is looking to rebuild their innings.

Luxury for England! Stats suggest that Moeen Ali has been doing a commendable job for them in Powerplay 1. It drops a bit post that but then Adil Rashid takes the charge and has fared better in the middle phase of the game. Michael Atherton on air also brings out the point that wrist spinners have been ruling the roost in the shorter version of late and although their economy rate is on the higher side, they tend to pick wickets.
Defended off the front foot with the full face of the bat.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Punches the ball to the off side, from the front foot and takes a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Flighted delivery outside off and Stoinis lets it go.
Adil Rashid to roll his arms over.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Another block off the front foot for nothing.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Starts with a good looking punch. It was a touch short from the wicket-taker, outside off and the skipper cuts it through the cover region. The fielder chases the ball to the boundary, does well to stop it inside the line but messes it up while throwing it. His foot dragged the boundary rope behind when he dived to stop the ball and when he stood up to throw it back, he didn't keep in mind the actual line. As a result, boundary singlled by the umpire.
Tim Paine is the new batsman in.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Ali is the man for England. He bowls another loopy delivery on middle stump and outfoxed the left-hander with the trajectory. Marsh plays for the spin but misses it altogether as the ball straightens and crashes into his stumps. Another one bites the dust.
Flicks the floated delivery off his pads and gets a single.

Powerplay 2 signalled by the umpire. Now, England can have four fielders outside the circle. Although, I doubt they would prefer to do that. Trying to pressurize the batsmen at the moment. Moeen Ali to continue...
Full again and angling down the leg side, Marsh flicks it off his pads but fails to beat short fine leg. End of the first Powerplay and England will be pleased with the outcome.
Fullish and outside off, a nicely timed drive by Marsh but he found the mid off fielder.
Clips it off his pads, in front of square leg and a couple of runs added to the total.
Bottom edge by the batsman! The keeper takes it on one bounce.

Aerial but safe! Almost another wicket there for England. A length ball outside off, Marsh plays a drive on the up and it goes uppishly towards cover-point. There was a short extra cover in place and had that been a little towards his right that would have been a straightforward catch. Root was the fielder and his gestures show the same.
Edgy! Fuller in length around off, angling away from the new batsman, Stoinis brings his bat down in defense but it takes the outside edge and rolls to third man. They cross for a single.
The ball takes the outside edge, goes towards the slip region. They pick up a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman, presenting the full face of the bat.
Marcus Stoinis is the next batsman to the crease.

OUT! This was coming. Finch wasn't able to get hold of Ali. He tries to create something out of nothing and loses his wicket. Ali flights the delivery on off and gets it to drift a bit as well. Finch reveals all his stumps to make some room for himself. Tries to go inside out but only manages an outside edge to Mark Wood stationed at short third man.  He makes no mistake and this is a big blow to Australia. Smart bowling change by Morgan has resulted in a wicket.
Played from the front foot down the pitch for nothing.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Drives the tossed up delivery from the front foot for nothing.
Moeen Ali is into the attack.
Driven through mid off by the batsman for nothing.
Short and into the body of Marsh. He tries to fend it off at the last moment but it goes off his gloves to short fine leg. Adil Rashid there overruns a bit and they collect a single.
Drives it to the mid off region and scampers for a quick single.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Plays the good length delivery from the inside half of the bat. The ball rolls to the mid-wicket region and they take one.
Driven though mid off but the connection isn't right. The fielder stationed there collects it and saves runs for his team.
Defends the good length delivery from the front foot down the pitch.
Driven from the front foot through mid on for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. One run added to the total.

FOUR! Beautiful! This one looked too easy for Marsh. He clipped this one off his hips and the fielder at short square leg had no chance of even getting a hand on it. Wood went a touch too straight and got punished for erring in line.
On a shortish length, into the body and Marsh blocks it.

FOUR! Shot! Marsh is dealing in boundaries. He isn't letting the opportunities go. Gets a shortish delivery outside off, goes on his toes and punches it down the ground. The fielder at mid off dives but in vain as the ball rushes to the boundary.
Plays the good length delivery to mid-wicket and keeps the strike for the next over.
Another block. Marsh is looking to set himself for a longer innings it seems. Similar length and a similar looking block from the left-hander.
Blocks the good length delivery from his crease.

Nice looking drive again from Finch. Gets the fullish ball on off stump and presents the full face of the bat from the front foot. The ball goes to the mid off region, where Hales dives to his right and stops a boundary. End result, a single.
Similar delivery from Willey, keeping a check on Finch, who blocks it down the pitch.
On a short of a good length, on off stump and Finch punches it to the off side for nothing.
On a length and around off, Marsh blocks it from the crease to complete the over. A maiden by Wood, finally finding some rhythm.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Marsh has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Gets one on his pads but Marsh fails to put it away.
Straighter in line and it has been pushed down the ground to mid on.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Shoulders his arms to the delivery outside off.
FOUR! Full on off stump and Finch brings the straight bat down to play through the line from the foot. The ball pierces through the covers and goes to the boundary in a flash.
The batsman gets a bottom edge of the bat on that one. One run added to the total.
Lets the length ball outside off pass to the keeper.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. They have run through for a single.
WOW! That swung and swung sharply into the right-hander, who tries to poke from his crease and gets an inside edge on to his pads. They take two as the ball rolls to backward square leg.

An overpitched ball on the pads, it's been flicked with good timing through mid-wicket. Willey gives the chase and slides just before the fence to pull it back. The fielder who had run in from mid off does the rest. Three taken and that brings up 1000 ODI runs for Aaron Finch against England.
In the channel outside off, an easy leave made this time from Aaron.
A back foot punch from the crease but not in the gap at covers.
Extra bounce from a length around middle, Finch tries working it on the leg side but misses. He is hit high on the thigh pad.

FOUR! Wood is not getting it right. Pitches this one full and around off, Aaron is on the front foot in a flash as he drives it firmly back past the bowler for a boundary down the ground. Now, this is a challenge for Wood. Willey is swinging from the other end but he is not getting any. He needs to hit the splice of the bat more in that case and ruffle the batsmen with his pace.
Angling in a length ball around off, Finch offers a stout defense from the crease.

FOUR! Punished! Willey goes a touch short outside off and Marsh punishes him. He gets on top of the ball and punches it through the cover-point region for another boundary. Good end to the over for Australia.

FOUR! Similar delivery which got the Travis Head's wicket but Marsh played it much better. He came closer to the ball, got his bat in line and creamed the cover drive for a boundary to get off the mark.
Plants his front foot forward and defends it in the ground for nothing.
Marsh lets the good length delivery go to the keeper.

OUT! Too easy. But kudos to Willey. He kept it on a fullish length, wide outside off and enticing the batsman to go for the expansive drive, who falls prey to it. The ball swings in the air and off the pitch, going away from Head who flashes his bat hard from the crease without any footwork. He gets an outside edge to the first slip region where Bairstow takes it easily. Australia lose their first wicket in the second over.
Defends the good length delivery from the crease.
David Willey starts the proceedings from the other end.
Another defense off the similar delivery from Finch to end the over.
Gets behind the line of the good length delivery and defends it from the middle of the bat.
Gets too straight and down the leg side. Umpire stretches his arms and signals a wide.
Gets behind the line of the length delivery and pushes it back to the bowler.

Shot! Nice looking punch from the back foot by Head. Wood gets even shorter and keeps it outside off, the batsman stays tall in his crease and punches the ball through the cover region. They take three from the vacant area.

Pitching on short of a good length, coming into the left-hander and gets the inside half of the bat. They take two while the mid-wicket fielder gets the ball and throws it back. Travis is off the mark as well.
Starts with a good length delivery on the off stump and Finch punches it to mid off from the front foot. Takes a quick single and opens his account.
Players are making their way out in the middle. Aaron Finch and Travis Head walk out and the former will take the strike while Mark Wood will get his hands on the first new ball for England.

TOSS - Australia win the toss and they are going to bat first. Michael Neser makes his international debut, while Aaron Finch and Travis Head are expected to open the innings. England are going with the expected XI, the only change being Jos Buttler returning to the playing XI.

On the other hand, England are currently top-ranked team in the ODI rankings. They have a settled team, an experienced leader in the form of Eoin Morgan, and they have played some exceptional cricket in the last 18 months. A hiccup in the last match against Scotland must have been frustrating but the management shouldn't be too worried about that. Sure they know they have a few areas to improve in order to become invincible and that can be put to test today. A mouth-watering contest is in store considering the history these two nations share. The English supporters won't make it easy for the visitors or their respective supporters. Stay tuned for exciting times ahead!

Hello and welcome to the coverage of the game between England and Australia from Kennington Oval, London. This is the first match for Australia after the debacle in South Africa earlier this year. They have revamped the whole squad with the appointment of a new skipper, Tim Paine and new head coach, Justin Langer. Big names are missing from the squad for obvious reasons and new faces have been handed the duties. Australia are looking to rise from 'the Ashes' and turn a new chapter in their history.
